content:
Your Routine Looks Right — So Why Isn't It Working?

Skincare mistakes are surprisingly common because most of them feel logical on the surface. Over-washing feels hygienic. Skipping SPF on cloudy days feels reasonable. Here's where things often go wrong.

Mistake 1: Using Too Many Active Ingredients at Once

Layering multiple actives — retinol, AHAs, vitamin C, niacinamide — without understanding how they interact can cause irritation, breakouts and a damaged skin barrier. More is not more in skincare.

What to do instead: Pick one or two actives appropriate for your main skin concern and use them consistently for at least 8 weeks before evaluating. Introduce new actives one at a time.

Mistake 2: Skipping Sunscreen on Cloudy Days

UV damage accumulates year-round, on cloudy days and even indoors near windows. This is the single most evidence-backed cause of premature skin ageing.

What to do instead: Apply SPF 30 or higher every morning as the last step of your routine, regardless of the weather. It takes less than 30 seconds.

Mistake 3: Aggressively Cleansing Oily Skin

If your skin is oily and you strip it with harsh cleansers, it responds by producing even more oil to compensate. This is called rebound sebum production.

What to do instead: Switch to a gentle, low-pH cleanser. Your skin should feel comfortable after cleansing — not tight, not squeaky clean.

Mistake 4: Not Giving Products Enough Time

Most skincare products require 8–12 consistent weeks before measurable results become visible, especially actives like retinol or vitamin C. Many people give up after 2 weeks.

What to do instead: Set a realistic 8-week trial for any new product. Take a photo on day 1 and day 56 for objective comparison.

Mistake 5: Touching Your Face Frequently

The hands carry bacteria, pollutants and oils that transfer to the skin with every touch. This is a significant but underestimated source of breakouts.

What to do instead: Practise mindful face-touching awareness. Clean your phone screen regularly. Never pick at breakouts.

Mistake 6: Using the Wrong Moisturiser for Your Climate

A heavy cream that works in winter can clog pores in summer humidity. Climate and season both affect what your skin barrier needs.

What to do instead: Assess your skin seasonally. A lighter gel moisturiser for summer and humidity; a richer cream for air-conditioned environments or winter.

Where to Start

Don't overhaul everything at once. Fix the mistake that resonates most with your current skin experience, and give it 30 days before making another change.
